preserved_prior_result: Crystal r1 remains archived at1/3 with two physical failures. The r2 source includes the moving-electrode conversion solved by that passer and instead neglects finite-load electric backaction. No old or new model evaluation was performed.

physics.scales: S lateral reference cells, N cells through slab, a0 reference length, q0 positive charge, E0 cell energy. C0=epsilon*a0*S/N; cL=CL/C0. Keep cL fixed in the macroscopic limit and CL fixed during the subsequent deformation. q=Q_top/(q0*S). Fixed known electrical coupling g=q0^2/(epsilon*a0*E0)=1.
physics.reduced_model: For c=det(F)|F^(-T)e3|^2, total per-cell energy is W0/E0+g[(q-s3)^2/c+q^2/cL]/2. Minimize charge to get q=cL*s3/(c+cL) and add g*s3^2/[2(c+cL)] to W0. The source solves W0 alone, then applies the exact same electrode charge/divider and its geometry derivative. Positive added curvature is the reciprocal field feedback that source omits.
physics.reference: Separate seven unknowns are s(3), lab normal electric field e, voltage v and crystal/load face charges qc,qL. Set b=|F^-T e3|, A=det(F)b and n=F^-T e3/b. Maxwell boundary charge gives qc=s3-A*e; potential drop gives v=-e/b; load gives qL=cL*v; each isolated node is neutral, qc+qL=0. Internal equilibrium includes g*e*F^T*n. The solver uses these equations jointly, never the reduced divider or Hessian, and obtains response from a fourth-order finite deformation difference of qc.
physics.reference_scope: This is an exact uniform macroscopic Maxwell problem, not a spatial mesh simulation of microscopic ionic fields. W0 already includes their zero-macroscopic-field free energy. The reference independently solves field/node/internal-force equations and differences charge, while sharing the specified constitutive energy. For ideal-short reference checks, v=0 replaces the load relation; qL then denotes compensating transferred charge rather than a finite capacitor face.
physics.sign: Positive measured current enters the top crystal electrode. Its connected load face has opposite free charge; the macroscopic field is positive upward when s3>0 in the loaded examples, with negative top-minus-bottom voltage. The energy and direct Maxwell reference give the same sign.
physics.domain_proof: Original upper-triangular F/G/K domain retained, finite cL in[.5,2], plus ideal-short preparations. Convexity is continuous: K>0 plus a positive electrostatic quadratic yields unique equilibrium. Prior analytic component bounds keep the negative center within the material cell: x1<=.0672, x2<=.0549 in absolute value, and -.00125<=s3<=.48265. Numerical samples support but do not replace these bounds.

Another96 random interior F/G/K/cL controls are saved. Both models are linear in drive; oracle sign reversal is separately checked. This is not an interval error proof.

Forty-one noiseless fits include both K endpoints. Existing analytic monotonicity proves global identification; the numerical fits are not a uniqueness proof for arbitrary noisy observations.
coverage.noise: 512 saved draws:256 at nominal K1.06 and256 with one draw at each K in a uniform endpoint-inclusive sweep. These are two finite tests, not all possible noise or a uniform probability guarantee. All declared fit/prediction gates are applied individually.

coverage.dimensional_scaling: Six dimensional energy checks use N8/64/512 and S50/200, verifying Cb from actual area/gap and intensive electric energy. A counterexample column records how fixed dimensional CL makes cL grow with N; it is not the intended apparatus.
